questions.q: Two hill stations, Auli and Mussoorie, record night temperatures. A student notes that the sum of the two temperatures is -4 degrees C and that Auli minus Mussoorie is -10 degrees C. A school trip carries sleeping bags rated down to -10 degrees C. (a) Find the temperature of each station. (b) Auli minus Mussoorie is negative; say which station is colder and by how many degrees. (c) If both stations fall by 5 degrees C the next night, find the new temperatures. (d) Should the group choose Auli with these bags? Justify.
questions.a: (a) Auli = (-4-10)/2 = -7, Mussoorie = (-4+10)/2 = 3. (b) Auli is colder, by 3 - (-7) = 10 degrees C. (c) Auli -7 + (-5) = -12, Mussoorie 3 + (-5) = -2. (d) Not safely: -12 is below the -10 rating, so Auli needs warmer bags or the trip should pick Mussoorie.

Part (b): says Auli is colder and finds the gap 3 - (-7) = 10
Part (c): adds -5 to each to get -12 and -2
Part (d): compares -12 with -10 and decides with a reason

questions.q: Nina says: "Subtracting takes away, so a - b is always smaller than a." Do you agree? Test it with a = 6, b = 4 and with a = 6, b = -4.
questions.a: No. With b = 4: 6 - 4 = 2, smaller than 6. With b = -4: 6 - (-4) = 6 + 4 = 10, which is larger than 6. Subtracting a negative integer is adding its positive inverse, so the claim holds only when b is positive.
s: Computes 10 for b = -4 and compares with 6
Gives the verdict no with the reason that subtracting a negative adds

questions.q: True or False: Reena starts with 4 green tokens, removes 12 red tokens without adding anything, and says "I can do it, and 4 - (-12) = 4 - 12 = -8." Give the verdict and the reason or the correction.
questions.a: False. There are no red tokens in the bag to remove, so she must first add 12 zero pairs. After removing the 12 reds, 16 greens remain, so 4 - (-12) = 4 + 12 = 16. Her -8 is the value of 4 - 12.
s: Correction: add 12 zero pairs, remove the reds, 16 greens left, so 4 - (-12) = 16 (-8 is 4 - 12)

questions.q: The canteen at the annual day sells samosas. Each ordinary samosa sold gives a profit of Rs 3. A tray went slightly cold, so those samosas were sold cheaper at a loss of Rs 5 each (the loss is written as an integer). On day one the canteen sold 40 ordinary and 12 cold samosas; on day two it sold 25 ordinary and 18 cold ones. If the cold samosas had been thrown away instead, each would be a loss of Rs 8. (a) Find the result for day one. (b) Find the result for day two. (c) Find the result for the two days together. (d) For day two, compare selling the cold samosas with throwing them away and advise the canteen.
questions.a: (a) 40 x 3 + 12 x (-5) = 120 - 60 = +60. (b) 25 x 3 + 18 x (-5) = 75 - 90 = -15. (c) 60 + (-15) = +45. (d) Throwing away: 75 + 18 x (-8) = 75 - 144 = -69, which is worse than -15, so selling at the cheaper price is better, although day two still makes a loss.
s: Part (c): adds the days to get +45
Part (d): computes -69 for throwing away and recommends selling

questions.q: A school bookstall must return unsold notebooks. Supplier P charges a fee of Rs 6 for each returned notebook. Supplier Q charges Rs 9 for each returned notebook but gives back a flat Rs 50 once. Fees are written as negative integers and the Rs 50 as +50. The stall expects between 14 and 20 returns. (a) Find the result with Supplier P for 14 returns. (b) Find the result with Supplier Q for 14 returns. (c) Find both results for 17 returns. (d) The stall expects 17 returns; which supplier should it choose, and for how many returns would the other supplier be better?
questions.a: (a) 14 x (-6) = -84. (b) 14 x (-9) + 50 = -126 + 50 = -76. (c) P: 17 x (-6) = -102. Q: 17 x (-9) + 50 = -103. (d) P, since -102 is better than -103. At 16 returns P is -96 and Q is -94, so Q is better for 16 or fewer returns.
s: Part (d): chooses P for 17 and notes Q is better up to 16 returns

questions.q: A worksheet says (-4) x 9 = 36. Using the times-9 pattern 2 x 9 = 18, 1 x 9 = 9, 0 x 9 = 0, show that this cannot be right.
questions.a: Continuing the pattern, the product falls by 9 each time the multiplier falls by 1: (-1) x 9 = -9, (-2) x 9 = -18, (-3) x 9 = -27, (-4) x 9 = -36. So (-4) x 9 = -36, not 36: a negative and a positive factor give a negative product.
s: Extends the pattern with a fall of 9 each step
Concludes 36 is impossible because one negative factor gives a negative product

questions.q: True or False: For every integer a, the product (-1) x a is a negative integer. Give the verdict and the reason or the correction.
questions.a: False. (-1) x a = -a, the additive inverse of a. For a = -9 it is 9 (positive) and for a = 0 it is 0, so it is negative only when a is positive.
s: Correction: (-1) x a = -a, e.g. (-1) x (-9) = 9 and (-1) x 0 = 0

questions.q: Isha says: "Multiplying an integer by a negative integer always gives a smaller number." Test this with 5 x (-2) and (-5) x (-2), and give your verdict.
questions.a: 5 x (-2) = -10 is smaller than 5, but (-5) x (-2) = 10 is larger than -5. So the claim is false: multiplying by a negative integer can give a larger number when the first factor is negative.
s: Compares each with the starting number (5 and -5)
Gives the verdict that the claim is false with a reason

questions.q:
Two integers p and q have the product 24, and p is negative with |p| less than |q|, both lying between -12 and 12.
(a) Explain why q must also be negative.
(b) List every possible pair (p, q).
questions.a: (a) A product of a negative and a positive integer is negative, but 24 is positive, so q cannot be positive; q is negative. (b) (-2, -12), (-3, -8), (-4, -6).
s: Part (a): explains with the sign rule that q is negative
Part (b): the three pairs and no others

questions.q: Two integers have product 91 and sum -20. One of them is -7, so the other is ___.

Two integers p and q, each of size at least 2 and at most 12 (so each is one of -12 to -2 or 2 to 12), have p x q = -36 or p x q = 36.
(a) List the pairs of sizes (|p|, |q|) that multiply to 36.
(b) How many ordered pairs (p, q) give -36?
(c) How many ordered pairs give +36?
(d) How many ordered pairs in all give -36 or 36?
(e) Why does each pair of sizes give exactly two ordered pairs for -36?
questions.a: (a) (3, 12), (4, 9), (6, 6), (9, 4), (12, 3). (b) 10 ordered pairs, e.g. (3, -12) and (-3, 12). (c) 10 ordered pairs, e.g. (-3, -12) and (3, 12). (d) 20. (e) For -36 exactly one factor is negative, and either p or q can be the negative one, so each pair of sizes gives two sign choices.
s: Part (a): the five pairs of sizes
Part (e): the negative factor can be p or q

questions.q: Ravi's worksheet on products of integers gives these answers: 1. 12 x (-5) = -60. 2. (-9) x (-4) = -36. 3. (-7) x 8 = -56. 4. (-6) x (-3) = -18. 5. 15 x (-2) = -30. The teacher gives +2 for a right answer and -1 for a wrong answer, and the pass mark is 5. (a) Which answers are wrong? (b) Write the correct values. (c) What is Ravi's score, and does he pass? (d) The teacher lets him correct some answers and be re-marked. What is the fewest he must correct to pass, and what is his score then?
questions.a: (a) Answers 2 and 4. (b) (-9) x (-4) = 36 and (-6) x (-3) = 18. (c) 3 right and 2 wrong: 3 x 2 + 2 x (-1) = 4, below 5, so he does not pass. (d) Correcting one answer gives 4 right and 1 wrong: 8 + (-1) = 7, which passes. Fewest corrections: 1 (score 7).
s: Part (a): answers 2 and 4 (two negatives give a positive)

questions.q: A game gives a player the score (-8) x n, where n is the number on the card drawn. The cards are numbered -3, -2, -1, 0, 1 and 2. For how many of these cards is the score greater than 10?

A school is choosing between two marking schemes for a 24-question quiz. Scheme X gives +5 for a correct answer and -3 for a wrong answer. Scheme Y gives +3 for a correct answer and -1 for a wrong answer. Gauri guessed everything: 12 correct and 12 wrong. Sahil answered only what he knew: 9 correct and none wrong. Tanvi was careful but not perfect: 16 correct and 4 wrong. The principal wants Sahil to beat Gauri by at least 10 marks, and wants Tanvi to lose no more than 10 marks to her wrong answers. (a) Find Gauri's marks under X and under Y. (b) Find Sahil's marks under X and under Y. (c) Find the marks Tanvi loses to her 4 wrong answers under X and under Y. (d) The principal says the lead of Sahil over Gauri matters more than Tanvi's limit. Which scheme should the school choose, and why?
questions.a: (a) X: 12 x 5 + 12 x (-3) = 24; Y: 12 x 3 + 12 x (-1) = 24. (b) X: 9 x 5 = 45; Y: 9 x 3 = 27. (c) X: 4 x (-3) = -12; Y: 4 x (-1) = -4. (d) Scheme X. It gives Sahil a lead of 45 - 24 = 21, which meets the wish of at least 10, and breaks Tanvi's limit by only 2 (loss 12 against 10). Scheme Y gives a lead of only 3 and fails the more important wish.
s: Part (d): compares the lead (21 and 3) and the loss (12 and 4) with 10, ranks the lead wish first and picks X

questions.q:
(a) Find (-7) x (-7) and 7 x 7.
(b) Can an integer multiplied by itself ever give a negative product? Give the reason.
questions.a: (a) 49 and 49. (b) No. If the integer is positive the product is positive; if it is negative, both factors are negative and the product is positive; if it is 0 the product is 0.
s: Part (b): no, with the sign rule for both cases

questions.q:

Reason (R): 6 x (-25) = -150 and (-6) x 25 = -150.
questions.a: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason explains the Assertion. The missing factors are -25 and 25, which are equal in size and opposite in sign.

Assertion is false, but the Reason is true

questions.q:
The quotient of two integers is -9 and the divisor is negative.
(a) Is the dividend positive or negative? Give the reason.
(b) Write two different divisions of this kind, with divisors between -10 and -2.
questions.a: (a) Positive. A positive dividend divided by a negative divisor gives a negative quotient, while a negative dividend would give a positive quotient. (b) Examples: 27 / (-3) = -9 and 45 / (-5) = -9 (also 36 / (-4), 54 / (-6), 63 / (-7), 72 / (-8), 81 / (-9), 90 / (-10)).
s: Part (a): positive, with the sign reason
Part (b): two correct divisions with divisors from -10 to -2

questions.q: A shop in Pune made a loss in two years. Year 1 loss was Rs 6,300 and year 2 loss was Rs 7,200; losses are written as negative integers and shared equally among the partners. Raju, a partner, can bear a loss of at most Rs 850 in any one year. The shop has 7 partners and can take in more, but then 9 partners in all. (a) Find each partner's year-1 share with 7 partners. (b) Find each partner's year-1 share with 9 partners. (c) Find each partner's year-2 share with 9 partners. (d) The shop could instead take in just one new partner (8 partners in all). Can the year-1 loss be shared equally in whole rupees among 8, and which plan should the shop choose if it wants Raju to stay? Justify.
questions.a: (a) (-6300) / 7 = -900. (b) (-6300) / 9 = -700. (c) (-7200) / 9 = -800. (d) With 8 partners, 6300 / 8 = 787.5 is not a whole number of rupees (and -6300 is not a multiple of 8), so equal sharing is impossible. With 9 partners the shares are -700 and -800, both within Raju's 850, while 7 partners give -900. So take in both new partners.
s: Part (d): shows 6300 is not a multiple of 8, compares 9 partners (700, 800) with 850 and 7 partners (900), and chooses 9

questions.q: Which of these quotients are integers: (-84) / 7, (-85) / 7, 96 / (-12), 100 / (-12)? Give the value of each integer one and say how you checked the others.
questions.a: (-84) / 7 = -12 and 96 / (-12) = -8 are integers. (-85) is not a multiple of 7 (7 x (-12) = -84 and 7 x (-13) = -91), and 100 is not a multiple of 12 (12 x 8 = 96 and 12 x 9 = 108), so the other two are not integers.
s: Shows the other two dividends lie between multiples of the divisor

Which of the statements is/are correct?

questions.q: Neha says: "For positive integers a and b, (-a) / b and a / (-b) are always equal." Do you agree? Test with a = 48 and b = 6.
questions.a: Yes. (-48) / 6 = -8 and 48 / (-6) = -8. Each has one negative and one positive number, so each quotient is negative with the same magnitude a / b = 8.
s: Gives the verdict yes with the one-negative reason

questions.q: Show that (-45) / 4 is not an integer, and write the two multiples of 4 on either side of -45 with their quotients when divided by 4.
questions.a: The quotient would need 4 x ? = -45, but 4 x (-11) = -44 and 4 x (-12) = -48, so no integer works. The multiples on either side of -45 are -44 and -48, and (-44) / 4 = -11, (-48) / 4 = -12.
s: Shows 4 x ? = -45 has no integer solution (-44 and -48)
States -45 is not a multiple of 4

questions.q:
The dividend is -144.
(a) Find the quotient for the divisors 8, -9 and -12.
(b) For how many divisors from -12 to 12 (leaving out 0) is the quotient positive?
(c) For how many divisors from -12 to 12 (leaving out 0) is the quotient an integer? List the divisors that fail the test from 1 to 12 and say why.
questions.a: (a) -18, 16 and 12. (b) The quotient is positive only for negative divisors: 12 of them. (c) The divisors 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12 divide 144 exactly, giving 8 positive and 8 negative divisors, 16 in all. From 1 to 12 the divisors 5, 7, 10, 11 fail, since 144 is not a multiple of them (and the same for their negatives).

questions.q:
Four students divide -72 as follows. Asha: (-72) / 9 = 8. Bela: (-72) / (-9) = -8. Chitra: 72 / (-9) = -8. Dev: (-72) / (-6) = 12.
(a) Which answers are wrong?
(b) Write the correct values.
(c) Use a multiplication check to show why Asha's answer cannot be right.
(d) State the sign rule that Asha and Bela broke.
questions.a: (a) Asha's and Bela's. (b) (-72) / 9 = -8 and (-72) / (-9) = 8. (c) 9 x 8 = 72, not -72, so 8 is not the missing factor; 9 x (-8) = -72. (d) A negative dividend with a positive divisor gives a negative quotient, and two negatives give a positive.
s: Part (d): states the rule for one negative and for two negatives

questions.q:
Anita divides a number by -6 and gets 16.
(a) Find the number.
(b) Her friend says dividing the same number by 6 also gives 16. Is the friend right? Show it.
questions.a: (a) The number is (-6) x 16 = -96. (b) No. (-96) / 6 = -16, the opposite sign: the dividend is negative and the divisor positive.
s: Part (b): finds -16 and says the friend is wrong

questions.q: A probe in a school science project sinks into a pond at a steady rate, written as a negative number of metres per minute. In the first setting it goes down 48 m in 6 minutes. In the second setting it goes down 90 m in 15 minutes. A probe that rises from depth uses a rise of 60 m in 5 minutes. The probe must go to -120 m and then rise back to 0 within a battery life of 25 minutes. (a) Find the rate of the first setting. (b) Find the rate of the second setting. (c) Find the time to go down to -120 m at each setting, and the time to rise back from -120 m. (d) Which setting can the project use? Justify.
questions.a: (a) (-48) / 6 = -8 m per minute. (b) (-90) / 15 = -6 m per minute. (c) Down: (-120) / (-8) = 15 min and (-120) / (-6) = 20 min. Rise rate 60 / 5 = +12 m per minute, so rising takes 120 / 12 = 10 min. (d) First setting: 15 + 10 = 25 min, within the battery life. Second: 20 + 10 = 30 min, too long. Use the first setting.
s: Part (d): totals 25 and 30 against 25 and chooses the first setting

questions.q: (-72) / 8 = -9, (-72) / 4 = -18, (-72) / 2 = -36 and (-72) / 1 = -72. Continue the pattern to predict (-72) / (-1) and (-72) / (-2), and say what happens to the quotient as the divisor falls.
questions.a: (-72) / (-1) = 72 and (-72) / (-2) = 36. As the divisor shrinks from 8 down to 1 the quotient grows in size (-9 to -72); once the divisor becomes negative the quotient turns positive, 72 and then 36. Check: (-1) x 72 = -72 and (-2) x 36 = -72.
s: Describes the change of sign and checks by multiplying

questions.q: A cold store is at 6 degrees C and its temperature changes by -4 degrees C every hour. How many hours does it need to reach -30 degrees C?

Cold store A cools by 4 degrees C every hour for 9 hours. Cold store B cools by 6 degrees C every hour.
(a) How many hours does B need for the same total change as A?
(b) How much sooner is that than A?
questions.a: (a) A's change is 9 x (-4) = -36. B needs (-36) / (-6) = 6 hours. (b) 9 - 6 = 3 hours sooner.

questions.a: Example: A trader's total loss is Rs 90 (-90) shared equally between 15 shops, so each shop has a loss of Rs 6, written -6.

A 20-question test gives +5 for each correct and -2 for each wrong answer, and all 20 are attempted. Ankit says he got exactly 50. Find the totals for 12 correct and for 13 correct answers, and use them to show that 50 is impossible.
questions.a: 12 correct and 8 wrong: 12 x 5 + 8 x (-2) = 60 - 16 = 44. 13 correct and 7 wrong: 13 x 5 + 7 x (-2) = 65 - 14 = 51. One more correct answer changes the total by 7, so the totals go 44, 51 and skip 50. No number of correct answers gives 50.

questions.q: A mining museum has two lifts. Lift 1 starts 30 m above ground and goes down at 5 m per minute. Lift 2 starts at ground level and goes down at 4 m per minute. A guide must reach the display at -140 m within 34 minutes. (a) Where is Lift 1 after 12 minutes? (b) After how many minutes does Lift 1 reach -140 m? (c) Where is Lift 2 after 34 minutes? (d) Which lift should the guide take, and why?
questions.a: (a) 30 + 12 x (-5) = -30. (b) (30 + 140) / 5 = 34 minutes. (c) 34 x (-4) = -136. (d) Lift 1 reaches -140 in exactly 34 minutes, the time limit; Lift 2 is only at -136 then. Take Lift 1.

questions.q:
A cold-room is at 28 degrees C and is cooled by 4 degrees C every hour for 9 hours. Then the power fails and the room warms by 2 degrees C every hour for 5 hours. Medicines must stay at or below -5 degrees C.
(a) Write one integer expression for the final temperature and evaluate it.
(b) Were the medicines safe at the end? By how many degrees is the room above or below the limit?
questions.a: (a) 28 + 9 x (-4) + 5 x 2 = 28 - 36 + 10 = 2 degrees C. (b) No. 2 is above -5, by 2 - (-5) = 7 degrees C. (After the cooling alone the room was at -8, which was safe.)
s: Part (b): not safe, 7 degrees above the limit

questions.q:
A 20-question test gives +3 for a correct answer and -1 for a wrong answer, and every question is attempted. Kabir gets 14 correct and Lata gets 16 correct.
(a) Find both totals.
(b) Each extra correct answer replaces a wrong one. By how much does it change the total, and does that agree with the gap between Lata and Kabir?
questions.a: (a) Kabir 14 x 3 + 6 x (-1) = 36; Lata 16 x 3 + 4 x (-1) = 44. (b) One more correct answer changes the total by 3 - (-1) = 4. Two extra correct answers give 8, which equals 44 - 36.
s: Part (b): change of 4 per answer, 2 x 4 = 8 agrees with 44 - 36

questions.q:

(a) Find the result of each week.
(b) In Week 4, 90 boxes are sold. How many returns would give neither profit nor loss?

A test has 25 questions with +3 for a correct answer, -1 for a wrong answer and 0 for an unanswered question. Hiral attempted all 25 and got 15 correct. (a) How many were wrong? (b) Find her total. (c) How many marks did she lose compared with the maximum 75? (d) She says that if she had left her 4 least-sure answers unanswered, all of which were wrong, her total would have been higher. Find the new total and say whether she is right. (e) By how much does her total change?
questions.a: (a) 10 wrong. (b) 15 x 3 + 10 x (-1) = 45 - 10 = 35. (c) 75 - 35 = 40. (d) 4 wrong answers become blank: 15 x 3 + 6 x (-1) = 39, higher than 35, so she is right. (e) It rises by 4.

questions.q: A tea stall earns Rs 6 on each special tea and loses Rs 4 on each spilt cup. (a) Find the result for 50 special teas and 30 spilt cups. (b) If spilt cups rise to 75 with the same 50 teas, find the new result and explain it.

True or False: In a 25-question test with +4 for each correct answer and -1 for each wrong answer, with every question attempted, Neha says a total of exactly 50 is possible, although 50 is not a multiple of 4. Give the verdict and the reason or the correction.
questions.a: True. With c correct answers the total is 4c + (25 - c) x (-1) = 5c - 25. For c = 15 this is 75 - 25 = 50: 15 correct and 10 wrong give 60 + (-10) = 50. The totals are multiples of 5, and 50 is one of them.
s: Reason: 15 correct and 10 wrong give 15 x 4 + 10 x (-1) = 50, the totals being 5c - 25

questions.q: A tea stall earns Rs 6 on each tea sold and loses Rs 9 on each spilt cup. After selling 90 teas, how many spilt cups give the stall neither profit nor loss?

In a school quiz of 25 questions the marking is +5 for a correct answer, -2 for a wrong answer and 0 for an unanswered question. Team A had 15 correct, 6 wrong and 4 unanswered. Team B had 17 correct, 8 wrong and none unanswered. Team C had 14 correct, none wrong and 11 unanswered. (a) Find Team A's score. (b) Find Team B's score. (c) Find Team C's score. (d) Name the winner. By how many marks does Team B lose, and how could B have won?
questions.a: (a) 15 x 5 + 6 x (-2) = 63. (b) 17 x 5 + 8 x (-2) = 69. (c) 14 x 5 = 70. (d) Team C wins by 1 mark over B. B lost 16 marks to wrong answers; leaving just one wrong answer unanswered would have made B 71, above 70.
s: Part (d): names C, 1-mark gap and shows 71 would win

questions.q: Sana says: "In a test with +4 for a correct and -2 for a wrong answer, a student who scores 0 must have exactly twice as many wrong answers as correct ones, or have answered nothing." Do you agree? Test it with 3 correct and some wrong answers that give a total of 0.
questions.a: Yes. For 3 correct: 3 x 4 = 12, so the wrong answers must give -12, which is 6 x (-2). 6 is twice 3. Each correct answer (+4) is cancelled by two wrong answers (2 x (-2) = -4). With nothing answered the total is 0 as well.
s: Finds 6 wrong answers give -12, twice the correct ones
Gives the verdict yes with the cancelling reason

(b) A product of 13 non-zero integers has 7 negative factors. State its sign.
(c) Two of its positive factors are replaced by their negatives. What is the sign now, and why?
(d) After that, one negative factor is replaced by its positive. What is the sign now?
questions.a: (a) -1 for 15 times (odd) and 1 for 16 times (even). (b) Negative, since 7 is odd. (c) Now 9 negative factors, still odd, so still negative (two sign changes cancel). (d) Now 8 negative factors, even, so the product is positive.

questions.q: In a board game every card multiplies your score by -1. Aarav starts with a score of 4 and ends with 4 again. Which could be the number of cards he drew?

Consider P = (-3) x (-7) x (-2) x 4 x 5, Q = (-3) x (-7) x (-2) x (-4) x 5 and R = (-1) x (-1) x (-1) x (-1) x (-1) x (-1) x 9.
(a) Which of the three products are positive?
(b) Q differs from P in one factor only. How does that change the sign, and why?
questions.a: (a) Q and R. P has 3 negative factors (odd) so it is negative; Q has 4 and R has 6, both even, so positive. (b) Changing the factor 4 to -4 adds one negative factor, making the count even, so the sign changes from negative to positive.
s: Part (a): Q and R, with negative counts 4 and 6 (P has 3)
Part (b): one extra negative factor flips odd to even, so the sign flips

questions.q: A 3 by 3 grid is made so that each cell is (row number) x (column number), with row numbers 3, -2, 5 and column numbers 4, -6, -1. The cells are 12, -18, -3 in row one, -8, 12, 2 in row two and 20, -30, -5 in row three. A student circles one cell, strikes its row and column, and repeats until three cells are circled. (a) Circle 12, 12 and -5 and find their product. (b) Circle -18, -8 and -5 and find their product. (c) Explain why the product is always the same. (d) Predict, without circling, the product for a grid with row numbers 2, -3, 4 and column numbers 5, -1, -2, and say whether it is larger than the first grid's product.
questions.a: (a) 12 x 12 x (-5) = -720. (b) (-18) x (-8) x (-5) = -720. (c) Each circled product is (3 x -2 x 5) x (4 x -6 x -1) in some order, = (-30) x 24 = -720. (d) (2 x -3 x 4) x (5 x -1 x -2) = (-24) x 10 = -240, which is larger than -720.
s: Part (c): one cell from each row and column so all row and column numbers appear once

questions.q:
Neha claims: "When the signs are mixed, the way you group three integers changes the product." Test her claim with a = -6, b = 5, c = -4.
(a) Find (a x b) x c.
(b) Find a x (b x c).
(c) Find (a x c) x b.
(d) Which grouping is easiest to do mentally, and why?
(e) Give your verdict on Neha's claim.
questions.a: (a) (-30) x (-4) = 120. (b) (-6) x (-20) = 120. (c) 24 x 5 = 120. (d) (a x c) x b, since (-6) x (-4) = 24 is a table fact and then 24 x 5. (e) Her claim is wrong: all groupings give 120, as the product of integers does not depend on grouping or order.
s: Part (d): picks a x c first with a reason

questions.q:
Look at these products: (-2) x (-3) x (-4); (-2) x (-3) x (-4) x (-5); 5 x (-1) x (-1); (-6) x 7 x (-8) x (-9).
(a) Which of them are positive?
(b) Find the value of each positive one.
questions.a: (a) The second (4 negative factors) and the third (2 negative factors); the first (3) and fourth (3) are negative. (b) (-2) x (-3) x (-4) x (-5) = 120 and 5 x (-1) x (-1) = 5.
s: Part (a): second and third, by counting negatives

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
1. The product of 6 negative integers is negative.
2. The product of 7 negative integers is negative.
3. A product of non-zero integers is negative whenever it has at least one negative factor.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.a: 2 only. Statements 1 and 3 are false: 6 negatives give a positive, and (-2) x (-3) = 6 is positive although it has negative factors.
o: 2 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3

questions.q: Dhruv writes (-2) x 5 x (-3) x (-1) x 4 x 6 = 720. Count the negative factors and show that his answer cannot be right. What is the correct value?
questions.a: The factors -2, -3 and -1 are negative: 3 negative factors (an odd number), so the product is negative. The magnitude is 2 x 5 x 3 x 1 x 4 x 6 = 720, so the correct value is -720, not 720.
s: States the product must be negative

questions.q: Find (-2) x (-3) x (-4) x (-5) and (-2) x 3 x (-4) x 5. What do you notice, and why does it happen?
questions.a: Both equal 120. The first has 4 negative factors and the second has 2; both counts are even, so the sign is positive, and the factors have the same sizes (2, 3, 4, 5), so the magnitude is the same.
s: Explains with even counts of negatives and equal magnitudes

questions.q: 6 x (-5) x 4 x (-3) = 360. Without multiplying again, predict the new product when (a) -5 is replaced by 5, and (b) -3 is replaced by -6.
questions.a: (a) The count of negatives falls from 2 to 1, so the sign flips and the magnitude stays: -360. (b) The sign stays positive and the factor 3 doubles to 6, so the product doubles: 720.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The product (-3) x (-4) x (-5) x (-2) x (-1) is positive.
Reason (R): A product of non-zero integers with an even number of negative factors is positive.
questions.a: Assertion is false, but the Reason is true. A is false: it has 5 negative factors so it is negative (-120). R is a true statement.
o: Assertion is false, but the Reason is true
Both Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason explains the Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true, but the Reason does not explain the Assertion
Assertion is true, but the Reason is false

questions.q: A product of seven non-zero integers is positive. The number of negative factors among them must be ___ (odd or even).
questions.a: even

questions.q: A product p has 9 non-zero integer factors, of which 4 are negative, so p is positive. One positive factor is replaced by the negative integer of the same size. The new product is
questions.a: negative, because it now has 5 negative factors
o: negative, because it now has 5 negative factors
positive, because 9 factors are non-zero
unchanged, because the sizes of the factors are the same
positive, because most of the factors are positive

questions.q: In a board game a card multiplies your score by -2 each time it is drawn. Dev starts with a score of 3. After how many draws is his score first greater than 100?
A teacher writes (-8) x (-3) x 5 x (-2) on the board. Four students rewrite it. Whose rewritten product has the same value?
o: 8 x 3 x 5 x 2

questions.q: Gita finds P = (-2) x (-3) x (-5) x (-1) x 4 and Q = 2 x 3 x 5 x 1 x (-4). Which is correct?
questions.a: P = 120 and Q = -120, so they are opposites
o: P = 120 and Q = -120, so they are opposites
P = -120 and Q = 120, so they are opposites
P = 120 and Q = 120, as the sizes are the same
P = -120 and Q = -120, as each has a negative factor

questions.q: In a card game, each card multiplies your score. Gita starts with 5 and draws the cards -2, 3 and -1 in order, then -4. (a) What is her score after the first three cards? (b) What is it after the fourth? (c) Three cards remain: -3, 2 and -5. She must draw exactly two of them (the order does not matter). Find the score for each possible pair. (d) Which pair should she draw to finish highest?
Write two different products of four non-zero integers, one with exactly one negative factor and one with exactly three negative factors, both equal to -24.
questions.a: Example: 2 x 3 x 4 x (-1) = -24 (one negative) and (-2) x (-3) x (-1) x 4 = -24 (three negatives). Either has an odd number of negative factors.
s: Gives a product of four integers with one negative equal to -24
Gives a product of four integers with three negatives equal to -24
States the odd count of negatives is why both are negative

questions.q: Lalit says: "If a product of integers has an odd number of negative factors, the product is negative." Do you agree? Test with (-2) x 3 x (-4) x (-1) x 5 and with (-2) x 0 x (-4) x (-1) x 5.
questions.a: Partly. The first has 3 negative factors and equals -120, which is negative. The second also has 3 negative factors but equals 0, because a factor is 0. So the claim holds only when all the factors are non-zero.
s: Verdict partly right: true only for non-zero factors

questions.q:
Pranav says: "Grouping never matters, so (10 - 4) - 3 = 10 - (4 - 3)."
(a) Test his statement.
(b) Show that grouping does not matter for the multiplication (-6 x 4) x 5 and (-6) x (4 x 5).
questions.a: (a) (10 - 4) - 3 = 3 but 10 - (4 - 3) = 9, so grouping matters for subtraction. (b) (-24) x 5 = -120 and (-6) x 20 = -120: equal, so grouping does not matter for multiplication of integers.
s: Part (a): 3 and 9, so his statement fails for subtraction

questions.q: Two shopkeepers near the school gate, Mohan and Sheela, are asked to bid for a stall at the annual fair for 8 weeks. Mohan's weekly entries in rupees, over five days, are +500, -300, +200, -450 and +150. Sheela's are +250, +250, -600, +400 and -100, but she must also pay a one-time fair fee of Rs 1,000 (written -1000). Each shopkeeper's weekly pattern repeats for all 8 weeks. (a) Find Mohan's weekly total and Sheela's weekly total. (b) Use the distributive property to find Mohan's total for 8 weeks: 8 x (500 + (-300) + 200 + (-450) + 150). (c) Find Sheela's total for 8 weeks including the fee. (d) The school will give the stall to the shopkeeper whose 8-week result is higher. Whom should it choose? Would the answer change at 10 weeks?
s: Part (d): chooses Mohan and notes the tie at 10 weeks

questions.q: Given that 15 x ((-8) + 3) = -75, write the value of (-15) x (8 - 3) without calculating, and say why.

A game-zone token machine gives green tokens worth +11 points and red tokens worth -7 points. A prize needs an exact score. Veena may use any number of each kind. To list the scores she writes the multiples of 11 (11, 22, 33, 44, 55 and so on) and subtracts multiples of 7. (a) Make a score of 15 using as few tokens as you can, and say how many you used. (b) Make a score of 4. (c) Make a score of -3. (d) The machine takes at most 9 tokens per prize. Can Veena win the 6-point prize? Search her listing for every way to 6 and justify.
questions.a: (a) 2 green and 1 red: 22 - 7 = 15, 3 tokens. (b) 1 green and 1 red: 11 - 7 = 4, 2 tokens. (c) 1 green and 2 red: 11 - 14 = -3, 3 tokens. (d) No. Checking every a + b of at most 9 tokens, none gives 11a - 7b = 6. The first way to 6 is 5 green and 7 red: 55 - 49 = 6, which is 12 tokens, more than 9.
s: Part (d): searches the combinations, finds the first way is 5 green and 7 red (12 tokens), over the limit, so no

questions.q:
A bakery chain compares two plans. Plan A earns Rs 14 and loses Rs 6 in every batch, for 40 batches. Plan B earns Rs 11 and loses Rs 2 in every batch, for 35 batches.
(a) Write each plan's net result as a product of a number and a sum, and evaluate it using the distributive property.
(b) Which plan is better and by how much?
s: Part (a): 320 and 315 using the distributive property

questions.q: Rani wants (-12) x 17. She writes 17 as 20 + (-3) and works out (-12) x 20 + (-12) x (-3). Which statement is correct?
questions.a: The method is valid and the value is -204

1. 38 x (-17) + 62 x (-17)

A token machine has only two kinds of coins, +5 and -10. Using the distributive property, show that +12 can never be made exactly. (Hint: 5 x a + (-10) x b.)
questions.a: Any total is 5 x a + (-10) x b = 5 x (a + (-2) x b) by the distributive property, so it is in the times-5 table (a multiple of 5). 12 is not a multiple of 5, so +12 cannot be made.
s: Writes the total as 5 x a + (-10) x b
Factors it as 5 x (a + (-2) x b) using the distributive property
Concludes 12 is not a multiple of 5

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The distributive property holds for integers, including negative ones.
Reason (R): (-2) x (4 + (-3)) and (-2) x 4 + (-2) x (-3) both equal -2.
questions.a: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but the Reason does not explain the Assertion. Both are true, but one example only checks the property; it does not explain why it holds for all integers.
o: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but the Reason does not explain the Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason explains the Assertion
Assertion is true, but the Reason is false
Assertion is false, but the Reason is true

questions.q: A cashier's five entries in rupees give the total 12 - 30 + 8 - 5 + 20 = 5. A second tally keeps the first entry 12 but reverses the sign of every other entry. Without adding all the entries again, what is its total?
Ritu writes: 6 x (5 + (-2)) = 6 x 5 + (-2) = 28. (a) Find her error. (b) Write the correct value, using both bracket-first and the distributive property.
questions.a: (a) She multiplied only the first number in the bracket by 6. (b) Bracket first: 6 x 3 = 18. Distributive: 6 x 5 + 6 x (-2) = 30 + (-12) = 18.
s: Part (a): says 6 was not multiplied with (-2)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
1. The distributive property a x (b + c) = a x b + a x c holds only when a, b and c are positive.
2. (-2) x (4 + (-3)) is equal to (-2) x 4 + (-2) x 3.
3. (-48) x (15 - 9) has the same value as 48 x (-15 + 9).
Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.a: 3 only. Statement 1 is false (it holds for all integers). Statement 2 is false: it should be (-2) x (-3). Statement 3 is true: both equal -288.
o: 3 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3

questions.q: Use the numbers 4, -3, 2 and -5 exactly once each, and each of the operations +, - and x exactly once, with brackets as you need. (a) Write an expression with the greatest possible value. (b) Write an expression with the least possible value. (c) Explain why the signs of your two answers are different.
questions.a: (a) ((-3) - (4 + 2)) x (-5) = (-9) x (-5) = 45. (b) (4 - (-3) + 2) x (-5) = 9 x (-5) = -45. (c) In (a) the bracket is negative and is multiplied by -5, giving a positive; in (b) the bracket is positive and multiplied by -5, giving a negative. The bracket magnitudes are equal (9).
s: Part (a): a valid expression with value 45
Part (b): a valid expression with value -45
Part (c): explains the sign difference with -5 as multiplier

questions.q: True or False: Rohit uses the rule -(a + b) = (-a) + (-b) with a = 8 and b = -3 and writes -(8 + (-3)) = (-8) + (-3) = -11. Rohit's working is correct. Give the verdict and the reason or the correction.
questions.a: False. The value is -(5) = -5. The additive inverse of b = -3 is +3, not -3, so the correct split is (-8) + 3 = -5.
s: Correction: the inverse of -3 is 3, so -(8 + (-3)) = (-8) + 3 = -5

questions.q: Three of these equations are correct uses of the distributive property. Which one is NOT?
Pranav says: "Since a x (b + c) = a x b + a x c, it must also be true that a + (b x c) = (a + b) x (a + c)." Do you agree? Test with a = 2, b = 3, c = 4.
questions.a: No. a + (b x c) = 2 + 12 = 14, but (a + b) x (a + c) = 5 x 6 = 30. The distributive property is for multiplication over addition, not addition over multiplication, so the claim fails.
s: Concludes no: the property works only in the form a x (b + c)

questions.q:
11 x (-9) = -99 and 11 x (-10) = -110.
(a) Use these two facts to find 11 x (-19) without multiplying 11 by 19.
(b) Check your answer by writing -19 as (-20) + 1 and distributing.
s: Part (a): -209 from adding the two products

questions.q: Fill in the blanks in three different ways with integers: ( __ + __ ) x __ = -24. At least one way must have a negative last number.
questions.a: Examples: (5 + 3) x (-3) = -24; ((-2) + (-10)) x 2 = -24; ((-1) + (-5)) x 4 = -24. A negative total times a positive number, or a positive total times a negative number, gives a negative product.
s: Gives one correct way with a negative last number
Gives two more correct and different ways
Explains the sign pattern that gives -24

questions.q: (a) Check the distributive property for (-3) x (7 + (-5)): find the value with the bracket first, and then by distributing. (b) Do the same for 7 x (6 + (-9)). (c) Ritu writes (-7) x ((-6) + 9) = (-7) x (-6) + 9 = 51. Find her error and give the correct value. (d) What do (a) to (c) suggest about the property for integers?
questions.a: (a) Bracket first: (-3) x 2 = -6. Distributing: -21 + 15 = -6. (b) 7 x (-3) = -21 and 42 + (-63) = -21. (c) She multiplied only the first number by (-7): the correct working is (-7) x (-6) + (-7) x 9 = 42 + (-63) = -21. (d) The property a x (b + c) = a x b + a x c holds for integers whatever their signs.
s: Part (c): spots that (-7) was not multiplied with 9
Part (d): states the property holds for integers

questions.q: Using the distributive property, 13 x (-47) + 13 x (-53) + 13 x 100 = ___.

Pooja writes 7 x (-18) = 7 x (-20) + 7 x (-2) = -154.
(a) Find the error in her splitting.
(b) Correct it and give the right product.
questions.a: (a) -18 is (-20) + 2, not (-20) + (-2) (which is -22), so the second term should be 7 x 2. (b) 7 x (-20) + 7 x 2 = -140 + 14 = -126.
